one_line_contribution: At a fixed episode budget on ALFWorld, what a multi-writer experience store adds to an in-context reader is claimed to be governed entirely by a pre-read, collection-log-computable statistic (the validation-weighted per-type success excess of the best writer over the reader), with writer count, writer diversity class and retrieval-time conflict each shown equivalent-to-null once that statistic and per-type item counts are held fixed, and all of it measured against the pool the reader could have collected itself at the same cost.
closest_prior_work: arXiv:2602.03794, 'Understanding Agent Scaling in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems via Diversity' (verified with s2cli paper; S2, 2026-02-03, 24 citations). Its thesis is literally the proposal's title claim in a different substrate: MAS performance is bounded by intrinsic task uncertainty and by how many *effective/complementary channels* the system accesses, not by agent count. The proposal's P2 headline ('headcount adds nothing once coverage is fixed') is therefore the outcome an already-published, already-cited framework predicts, and the proposal's dismissal of it as 'inference-time ensembles, not stored experience' concedes only the substrate. Second threat: arXiv:2604.03295, 'Scaling Teams or Scaling Time? Memory Enabled Lifelong Learning in LLM Multi-Agent Systems' (verified with s2cli paper; HF, 2026-03-27), which already reports non-monotonic scaling in team size specifically when experience is reused, i.e. already denies that headcount governs in a memory setting. What survives as novel is narrower than the title: the operationalization of coverage as a frozen pre-read statistic C, the matched-collection-budget self-pool denominator, and the orthogonalized manipulation. arXiv:2606.19911 (MATM, verified) pools producer trajectories for consumers but at unmatched cost with unstated producer heterogeneity, and arXiv:2210.08073 (verified, CoRL 2022, 33 cit) does demonstrator compatibility for trained policies, so neither pre-empts the estimand. Neither does arXiv:2603.02473 from the novelty card (write-strategy x retrieval crossing, single writer identity).
strongest_objection: The equal-coverage construction amputates the very mechanism headcount could act through, so P2's equivalence is cheap to affirm and the title overclaims what was tested. EC8 is built by stripping the six extra writers of items on every type where they exceed max(s_self, s_gptoss) and then equalizing per-type item counts to COV; EC4-prox/EC4-cap are restricted the same way. What is left varying between COV (N=2) and EC8 (N=8) is only which writer's name is attached to items filling identical per-type slots. 'More writers add nothing' has thus been reduced to 'shuffling item provenance within a type at fixed count and fixed type-level success adds nothing', which almost no one disputes and which the +/-6 band (the entire Gate-0 effect, and a third of the measured k3-static3 residual of +17.2) makes near-certain to affirm. This is the same defect the archived contributor_conflict_not_size was rejected for, with the sign flipped: there conflict was a property of the construction, here the *absence* of a headcount effect is. The arithmetic makes it worse: at B/8 = 444 episodes per writer, a writer's expected success-filtered items on a weak type such as heat are roughly 444/6 * 0.26 ~ 19 before the coverage restriction and the equalization, so several writer-type cells in EC8 will hold a handful of items or none, and with k=3 retrieval the eight-writer store is, at the item level, a two-writer store wearing eight labels. A second, related objection: P1's direction (a store carrying items on the reader's weak types beats one that does not) is close to a re-derivation of the on-disk Measurement A result, which already showed the expert bank's gain is carried by clean/heat/cool, precisely the reader's low-success types.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Manipulate coverage within a single writer so writer identity is not confounded with C: add DOM-go = self(B/2) + gpt-oss(B/2) restricted to the types where s_gptoss(t) <= s_self(t), item-count-equalized to COV. This is a filter on already-collected items, costs no extra collection, and makes COV vs DOM-go a clean coverage contrast with backbone, scaffold and phrasing held fixed; the present COV vs DOM contrast varies coverage and backbone together (gpt-oss-120b vs Qwen3 at T=1.2). (2) Run the headcount arm in the form a practitioner faces: eight writers with their coverage intact at B/8 versus two writers at B/2 with equal total items, reported alongside EC8, and let C predict the difference rather than being equalized away; report both the amputated and the intact contrast under the title. (3) Fix P4 as the entailment check indicates: pre-register a denominator gate (gain_expert - gain_SELF at or above ~30 net with its CI clearing that value, else P4 reported untested), or replace the 0.6 ratio with the paired difference gain_HCM-item - gain_expert tested for equivalence at +/-6. (4) Demote P6 explicitly to a descriptive statistic: with C identical by construction across COV/EC8/EC4-prox/EC4-cap/skel1/skelV, a large share of the 21 cells are ties and rho is a re-description of P1's contrast plus construction ties. (5) Tighten the equivalence band, or state plainly in the abstract that effects up to 5 net success points are not claimed absent.
missing_baseline: A budget-reallocated self pool: the reader collecting its own B episodes tilted toward the types where its own success is lowest (or the existing self pool per-type item-count-equalized), read at k=3. The reader's self pool is heavily type-skewed by construction (pick-and-place 0.81 vs heat 0.26 per the brief's Step 0), so COV's advantage over SELF may be nothing more than COV having items on the reader's weak types, which the reader can buy with its own budget by sampling more weak-type games rather than by recruiting a second writer. Without this arm, 'a population of writers adds coverage' is not shown to require a population: it is shown that a store with weak-type items beats a store without them. SELF(B) and self(B/2) do not supply it, because both inherit the same type skew. This omission is the more damaging because C is defined over only six ALFWorld types, so C is close to a re-parameterization of 'which types does the store cover', and the type-rebalanced self pool is the arm that separates 'coverage' from 'other writers'. Secondary omission: an oracle-retrieval or type-oracle store bounding how much of the headline gain is retrieval-side rather than store-side.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above average for this pipeline: three s2cli queries with hit counts, IDs, an explicit home-literature query, `paper` verification of its two load-bearing IDs, and an honest note that WebSearch was unavailable. I verified all six IDs its novelty argument rests on with `s2cli.py paper` (channel: the literature command, S2 and HF both ok): 2404.09982 Memory Sharing (S2, 2024-04-15, 33 cit), 2606.19911 MATM (S2, 2026-06-18), 2604.03295 Scaling Teams or Scaling Time (HF, 2026-03-27), 2602.03794 Understanding Agent Scaling via Diversity (S2, 2026-02-03, 24 cit), 2607.05844 StateFuse (HF, 2026-07-07), 2210.08073 Eliciting Compatible Demonstrations (S2, CoRL 2022, 33 cit). None could not be verified. My own queries, all answered by the literature command (WebSearch unavailable in this session, WebFetch blocked; no query needed channel (b)): [mechanism, --recent] 'value of shared experience memory as a function of number and diversity of contributing agent policies at matched collection budget' returned 14, nearest 2606.18829 GateMem (governance across principals, no writer-count manipulation), 2602.05965 LTS, 2602.03036 LatentMem, 2505.18279 Collaborative Memory - none matched-cost, none varying writer count; [mechanism, all time] 'does adding more contributing writers to a shared agent skill library help scaling number of contributors experience pool' returned 15, nearest 2604.08377 SkillClaw (aggregating many users' interactions into shared skills, but no count sweep and no self-pool control), 2601.04748 'When Single-Agent with Skills Replace Multi-Agent Systems and When They Fail' (scaling limits of skill libraries, not writer population), 2608.11888, 2605.23657 OpenSkillEval; [closest named method] 'Multi-Agent Transactive Memory retrieval of agent-generated artifacts across heterogeneous agent populations producer consumer' returned 12, confirming 2606.19911 as uniform pooling with no producer-count or matched-budget arm, plus 2605.04811 TreeMem (credit assignment across agents in a memory system - adjacent to C as a per-writer value statistic but post hoc from rewards, not pre-read from collection logs); [home literature] 'complementary skill coverage rather than number of models predicts ensemble gain diversity metric computed before combination' returned 12, nearest 2302.00704 Pathologies of Predictive Diversity in Deep Ensembles (capacity beats predictive diversity - the same shape of claim in the ensemble home literature, and a reference the proposal should cite and distinguish) and 2603.15276; [predictor] 'predicting in advance which stored trajectories will help a reader agent per-task-type success profile predictor of retrieval gain' (--recent) returned 10, nearest 2608.14036 'Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work-Until They Don't' (skills work by procedural anchoring rather than injecting missing knowledge - a direct threat to the interpretation of C, since it predicts gain where the reader lacks *stability*, not where it lacks *success*, and the proposal neither cites nor arms against it) and 2607.10608 The Compliance Trap; [matched cost] 'matched collection budget comparison self-collected trajectory pool versus pooled experience from other agents ALFWorld equal number of episodes' (--recent) returned 11 with nothing relevant - reported as empty, not as evidence of novelty. So the matched-cost self-pool denominator and the frozen pre-read C appear genuinely unclaimed, but the headline 'not headcount' half of the claim is anticipated conceptually by verified 2602.03794 and empirically by verified 2604.03295, and the proposal's check names both while under-weighting them.
